To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ‘Japanese best practices’ model is a good fit with the work organization, the manufacturing practices, and the performance of the Singaporean plants of Japanese firms; (2) Japanese firms in Singapore are more likely than their US and UK counterparts to rely heavily on expatriates, and (3) there are no significant relationships between the HRM practices cluster and either the work organization cluster or the performance of the plants.

the manufacturing practices of Japanese companies in Singapore are strongly influenced by their Japanese parent companies, but that the human resource management practices of these companies are strongly influenced by host country norms, and that the work organization practices are a compromise between these two forces.

the Japanese manufacturing system has been transferred successfully to Singapore in the sense that the manufacturing practices are similar in both countries, but the HRM practices are different, and this is consistent with the literature on transplants in other developed countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of the Japanese best practice model of work organization and manufacturing practices to Singapore.
the transfer of the Japanese best practice model (or lean production) to the host country of Singapore, with a particular emphasis on the role of HRM in this process.
the question of whether Japanese companies can transfer the ‘best practices’ of Japanese manufacturing to overseas affiliates and, if so, what factors facilitate or hinder such transfers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in Singapore, the Japanese best practice manufacturing model has been transferred with a high degree of integrity, but that the HRM model has been adapted in a manner consistent with host country norms.

the Japanese best practice model has been successfully transferred to Singapore in the manufacturing practices and work organization areas, but that the HRM practices of Japanese companies in Singapore have been adapted to host country norms.
the Japanese best practice model has been successfully transferred to Singapore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transfer of Japanese best practice is more successful when it is accompanied by the transfer of Japanese management practices, and when the Japanese managers are able to maintain a strong influence over the local workforce, and that this influence is most effectively exercised through expatriate managers.
Japanese transplants to Singapore have been very successful in adopting the ‘lean’ manufacturing model, but have had to adapt their HRM practices to the local context.
the Japanese manufacturing system is being transferred to Singapore with the work organization and manufacturing practices conforming closely to the Japanese model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Japanese best practice model of work organization, manufacturing practices and performance outcomes has been transferred to Singapore in a relatively intact form, but that the HRM practices associated with the Japanese best-practice model have not.
, while the Japanese best practice model has been successfully transferred to Singapore, it has been modified and adapted to fit the local context.
, while there is a strong relationship between work organization, manufacturing practices and performance outcomes, HRM practices are less related to the other variables in the model.
